title: Reference to Abstract Objects in Discourse
abstract: Develops a semantic theory of reference to abstract entities such as propositions, facts, events, and situations, providing a foundational treatment of how discourse introduces and subsequently refers to such objects.

admission.reason: Claim is out of scope for this reading round: the abstract provides a semantic ontology for propositions, facts, events, and situations, but it does not show a mechanism for identifying antecedent spans, resolving anaphoric expressions, or determining response scope. The ontology may be useful background, but the stricter gate requires a capability that materially strengthens one of the resolution streams.

title: Resolving Pronominal Reference to Abstract Entities
abstract: Introduces a computational approach for resolving pronouns that refer to abstract entities as well as ordinary individuals, explicitly constructing candidate abstract referents from preceding discourse.
venue: Proceedings of the 40th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

admission.reason: Evidence duplicates stronger admitted coverage of abstract-anaphora resolution. The abstract does show construction and resolution of abstract referents, but the admitted VERIFIED 2017 mention-ranking paper provides a more modern antecedent-span ranking formulation, while the admitted 2018 survey supplies broader historical coverage. Because this candidate is UNCHECKED and does not show a distinct capability needed by the project, it does not justify another reading slot.

title: Scoring Coreference Chains with Split-Antecedent Anaphors
abstract: Generalizes coreference evaluation metrics to structures containing split antecedents; the resulting framework supports evaluation of multi-antecedent plural reference and has also been applied in shared-task settings involving discourse deixis.

admission.reason: Topic words match but the capability does not sufficiently strengthen the resolution stream: this paper generalizes evaluation metrics for split-antecedent structures rather than resolving references. Domain-specific evaluation could become useful later, but the present reading slot is better spent on an actual multi-antecedent resolver; general evaluation concerns also overlap Topic 10.

title: Neural Anaphora Resolution in Dialogue Revisited
abstract: Revisits neural dialogue anaphora resolution using a span-based architecture and systematic hyperparameter optimization across identity, bridging, and discourse-deixis tracks.

admission.reason: Evidence duplicates papers already admitted for dialogue discourse deixis. The abstract mainly revisits a span-based neural architecture and hyperparameter optimization across identity, bridging, and discourse-deixis tracks; the admitted end-to-end discourse-deixis paper provides the more directly relevant anaphor-plus-antecedent-span capability, and the admitted CODI-CRAC shared-task paper provides the dialogue task and dataset framing.

title: Studies on the Semantics of Questions and the Pragmatics of Answers
abstract: Develops a systematic formal account of question semantics and the pragmatics of answers, including how propositions partition possibilities and contribute to resolving information requested by a question.

admission.reason: Evidence duplicates the admitted F4 foundation rather than adding a clearly distinct capability. The abstract describes broad question semantics and pragmatics of answers, while the admitted question-semantics, QUD, and question-resolution papers already cover possible answers, discourse organization, and contextual question resolution. The abstract does not show a more specific treatment of partial or multi-question response scope that would justify an additional slot.

title: Free the Plural: Unrestricted Split-Antecedent Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Develops end-to-end split-antecedent resolution without relying on gold identification of plural anaphors, allowing one anaphoric expression to be linked to multiple separately introduced antecedents.

admission.reason: Evidence duplicates the admitted split-antecedent resolver. This paper provides end-to-end split-antecedent resolution, but the admitted 2021 system covers split antecedents together with ordinary single-antecedent resolution in one end-to-end architecture using predicted mentions. The abstract does not show a project-critical capability beyond that coverage.

title: Anaphora Resolution in Dialogue: System Description (CODI-CRAC 2022 Shared Task)
abstract: Describes a dialogue anaphora system whose discourse-deixis component combines antecedent resolution with prediction of the anaphoric expression's type, alongside related bridging and identity-resolution components.

admission.reason: Evidence duplicates admitted F2 coverage. The described system combines discourse-deixis antecedent resolution with anaphor-type prediction, but the admitted end-to-end EMNLP discourse-deixis paper already supplies the stronger core capability, while the admitted CODI-CRAC shared-task paper supplies the task definition and benchmark context. The system-description abstract does not show an additional response-scope mechanism.

title: Questions in Montague English
abstract: Develops a formal semantic treatment of questions in which questions are associated with sets of possible answers, providing an influential foundation for later work on answerhood and question resolution.

admission.reason: Evidence duplicates the admitted formal answerhood foundation. Associating questions with sets of possible answers is important historically, but the admitted question-semantics and question-resolution papers already provide that machinery together with more direct relevance to partial and contextual resolution. The abstract does not show an additional capability needed for response-scope decisions.

title: Event-building through Role-filling and Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Explores event representations in discourse and the interaction between event construction and anaphora resolution, including cases in which event descriptions provide antecedents for subsequent reference.
venue: 29th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

admission.reason: Topic words match but the abstract does not show a sufficiently specific capability beyond stronger admitted event-reference evidence. It discusses event representations and their interaction with anaphora, but does not establish an explicit antecedent-ranking, span-resolution, clustering, or no-link mechanism comparable to the admitted event-reference and event-anaphoricity papers.

title: Dialogue Acts, Synchronizing Units, and Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Studies anaphora in spontaneous dialogue and proposes an account linking dialogue structure and synchronizing units to the interpretation of anaphoric expressions, including references whose antecedents are not simple nominal entities.

admission.reason: Topic words match but the abstract does not settle the project-critical capability. It links dialogue structure and anaphora and mentions antecedents that are not simple nominal entities, but it does not show that discourse-deictic or propositional links are represented separately from ordinary coreference, nor that exact antecedent spans or unsupported cases are resolved. Stronger F2 candidates already demonstrate those capabilities.

title: Neural Anaphora Resolution in Dialogue
abstract: Describes neural systems for the CODI-CRAC dialogue shared task, including a discourse-deixis component that identifies and resolves anaphoric references to prior discourse material.

admission.reason: Evidence duplicates admitted dialogue discourse-deixis coverage. This system implements the CODI-CRAC dialogue task, but the admitted shared-task paper supplies the benchmark definition and the admitted 2022 end-to-end discourse-deixis paper supplies the more directly relevant resolver. The abstract does not show a distinct response-scope capability warranting another reading slot.

title: Constrained Multi-Task Learning for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Uses constrained multi-task learning for event coreference together with related subtasks including event anaphoricity determination, providing transferable machinery for no-link decisions and antecedent-oriented event resolution.

admission.reason: Evidence duplicates the admitted event-coreference transfer paper. This candidate also combines event coreference with event-anaphoricity-related subtasks, but the admitted 2017 joint model already directly supplies the no-link/anaphoricity mechanism needed for transfer. The abstract does not show a distinct antecedent-scope capability that would justify another slot.
